name: Valley of the Gods BLM Free Primitive Camping Area

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management - Monticello Field Office

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 consecutive days max stay within 28-day period
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted at designated pullouts along the 17-mile unpaved Valley of the Gods loop road. Vehicles must stay on existing pullouts.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Desert soil pack-out strictly recommended or cat-hole 6 inches deep in dry sandy washes, 200 feet from drainages. Pack out all toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace pack-it-in pack-it-out. Zero trash bins.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Bring your own firewood. Gathering desert vegetation is strictly illegal.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires in elevated metal fire pans or existing rock rings only. Extinguish cold to touch.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved dirt and gravel desert loop road (Valley of the Gods Road / UT-262 connector)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard dirt road with sandy wash crossings and rocky dips. Can turn muddy and impassable during heavy rainstorms.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance car or CUV/SUV recommended (Normal low clearance 2WD cars can complete the loop in dry weather if driven slowly, but high clearance preferred for dip washes)

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 4G LTE (15-35 Mbps download on elevated pullouts)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Massive sandstone monoliths create localized signal shadows)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 65-80°F, high desert winds (20-35 mph gusts), pleasant spring sun.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot (95-104°F), intense desert solar radiation, July-August afternoon monsoon flash floods.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Premier boondocking season (70-82°F daytime, 40-50°F nights), clear dry skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cool 40-50°F daytime, freezing nights (20-30°F), rare dustings of snow on red sandstone towers.

dangers_and_hazards: Flash flooding filling dry washes during summer monsoons
Dehydration and intense desert summer heat
Midget Faded Rattlesnakes (Crotalus concolor) in rocky crevices

common_human_made_sounds: Infrequent overlanding rig driving slowly past on dirt road
Wind blowing past massive sandstone towers

human_demographics_and_culture: Full-time digital nomads, landscape photographers, Monument Valley travelers, overlanders, and solitude seekers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Navajo (Diné) oral traditions revere the red sandstone monoliths of Valley of the Gods as sacred stone warriors turned to rock by the Creator to protect the sacred Dinétah lands.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: High quartz red sandstone earth energy, profound ancient silence, breathtaking cosmic night skies.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Valley of the Gods Monolith Exploration Route
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Winding desert path past iconic sandstone formations (Rooster Butte, Setting Hen, Battleship)

public_reviews_summary: Often called 'Mini Monument Valley without the fees or crowds'. Jaw-dropping red rock monolith views, total peace, and great cell service.
other_data: Bortle Class 2 night sky. 100% solar power panel output.

name: Hole-in-the-Rock Road BLM Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management (BLM) - Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Free BLM Dispersed Camping Permit available at Escalante Interagency Visitor Center (zero cost)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed camping at established pullouts along Hole-in-the-Rock Road (BLM 200). Must carry portable toilet system or WAG bags in slot canyon zones.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Portable toilet system or pack-out human waste (WAG bags) mandatory in Escalante canyon country. Digging cat-holes strictly prohibited in narrow desert wash areas.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Pack-In / Pack-Out. Zero trash left in desert.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Must bring your own firewood. Gathering wood on Grand Staircase-Escalante BLM land is prohibited.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires must be contained in metal fire pan. Fully extinguish before leaving.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Summer desert fire restrictions active June through August.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Unpaved Dirt / Washout Desert Road (Hole-in-the-Rock Road / BLM 200)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Severe washboard dirt, clay mud when wet, flash flood wash crossings.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: High clearance 2WD or 4x4 recommended; careful standard 2WD cars can reach first 5 miles in dry conditions.

nomad_connectivity_rating.overall_rating: Fair near Highway 12 / Weak down road
nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE near highway junction; SOS further down road
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Sandstone slickrock mesas block signals in deep washes)

amenities: Slot Canyon Trailhead Access (Peek-A-Boo / Spooky Slot access)

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-72°F, prime desert hiking weather, clear sunny skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 88-102°F, intense desert heat, afternoon monsoon flash flood risk in slot canyons.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: 60-78°F, golden autumn cottonwoods in Escalante river canyon, perfect desert temps.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 25-45°F, freezing desert nights, dustings of snow on red slickrock.

dangers_and_hazards: Monsoon flash floods in slot canyons (check weather forecast at visitor center)
Severe washboard road causing vehicle rattles and damage
Dehydration in dry high desert heat
human_demographics_and_culture: Ancestral Puebloan & Fremont lands, slot canyon hikers, desert wanderers, vanlifers.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Grand Staircase slickrock features ancient Fremont rock art and sacred petroglyphs honoring water and desert spirits.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound red rock desert mana, vast silent horizons, world-class dark night skies.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Peek-A-Boo and Spooky Slot Canyons Loop
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Narrow sandstone slot squeezes, arches, slickrock scrambles

public_reviews_summary: Unbelievable red rock desert primitive camping outside Escalante. Epic slot canyon hiking, free BLM permit, and solid cell service near the highway entrance.
other_data: BLM Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument. Free permit required.

name: Wedge Overlook BLM Dispersed Primitive Camping

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management (BLM) - Price Field Office

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - Public BLM Land Dispersed Primitive Camping (zero fees)
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted at designated pullouts along Wedge Overlook Road (Buckhorn Draw / San Rafael Swell). Portable toilet recommended.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Portable toilet system or pack-out human waste (WAG bags) recommended on canyon rim. Dig cat-hole 6-8 inches deep in desert soil 200ft from rim edges.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Must bring your own firewood. Gathering wood on BLM rim lands is prohibited.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires must be contained in metal fire pan. Fully extinguish before leaving.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Summer desert fire restrictions active June through August.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Paved UT 155 to graded gravel dirt BLM roads (Buckhorn Draw Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Graded gravel, washboard dirt, easily drivable in dry weather.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: Accessible by standard 2WD low clearance passenger cars in dry weather.

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 3-4 bars 4G LTE along 6,200ft Wedge Overlook canyon rim
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Low along high open canyon rim; high inside deep Buckhorn Draw canyon

amenities: 'Little Grand Canyon' Red Sandstone Panorama Views

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: 55-72°F, prime desert canyon hiking weather, clear blue skies.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: 85-98°F, warm sunny desert canyon days, breezy nights.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: 60-78°F, golden autumn cottonwoods in canyon bottom, ideal desert temps.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: 22-42°F, freezing desert nights, dusting of snow on red canyon cliffs.

dangers_and_hazards: Sheer 1,000ft canyon cliff drop-offs at Wedge Overlook (watch footing near rim)
Flash floods in narrow slot draws during summer thunderstorms

common_human_made_sounds: Occasional 4x4 engine on distant dirt road

human_demographics_and_culture: Fremont Culture ancestral lands, San Rafael Swell ranchers, desert nomads, rock art stewards.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Known as the 'Little Grand Canyon of Utah'. Buckhorn Draw features world-famous ancient Fremont barrier-canyon style petroglyph panels.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Profound 1,000ft red sandstone canyon rim energy, breathtaking sunrise light.

nearby_hiking_trails.features: 1,000ft canyon rim panoramas, desert slickrock, ancient juniper groves

public_reviews_summary: Utah's single best free rim camping spot. 1,000ft canyon drop-off views over the Little Grand Canyon, blazing cell internet on the rim, and free BLM access.
other_data: BLM San Rafael Swell Recreation Area. Free dispersed primitive camping.

name: Comb Ridge Primitive Dispersed BLM Zone - Bears Ears National Monument

management_agency.name: Bureau of Land Management (BLM) - Monticello Field Office

rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 14 days maximum stay limit within a 28-day window
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping allowed along Comb Wash dirt road (Butler Wash & Comb Wash corridor). Do not touch or disturb archaeological sites. Leave No Trace.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Pack out solid human waste using Portable Toilet / WAG bags due to fragile desert soil. Alternatively bury 6-8 inches deep 200 ft from wash.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and down pinyon-juniper wood.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires permitted in cleared stone rings. Extinguish cold with water.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Subject to BLM Stage 1 & Stage 2 dry desert fire bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Gravel and dirt wash road (Comb Wash Road)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Graded dirt/sand road with washboard ruts and dry wash crossings.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: CUV, SUV, or 2WD high clearance car fine in dry weather; 4WD required after flash rains.

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2 bars 4G LTE on open wash flats, spotty under cliff walls

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: Ideal desert spring weather (65-76°F) with blooming desert wildflowers.
seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Hot desert summer (90-98°F) with afternoon red rock monsoon thunderstorms.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Perfect dry autumn weather with golden cottonwood trees in wash.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Cold high desert winter (20-40°F) with snow-dusted red cliffs.

dangers_and_hazards: Flash Floods in Wash Bed (Never camp in dry wash bottoms)
human_demographics_and_culture: Ancestral Puebloan, Navajo (Dine), Hopi, Ute, and San Juan county outdoor conservation culture.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Dine, Hopi, and Ute sacred traditions honor Comb Ridge as a living ancestral backbone ('Bears Ears' landscape).
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: Towering 800-foot red sandstone monocline radiating 300 million years of earth history.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Comb Wash Canyon & Monarch Cave Trail
nearby_hiking_trails.features: Red sandstone monocline cliff walls, dry wash canyon, cliff alcoves

public_reviews_summary: Mind-blowing red rock canyon solitude in Bears Ears National Monument with free BLM camping.
other_data: Pack in all drinking water and treat archaeological sites with deep respect (Visit With Respect guidelines).

name: Dixie National Forest Boulder Mountain Primitive Zone

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Dixie National Forest (Fremont River Ranger District)

rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping allowed along Hells Backbone Road and forest service roads. Camp 100 ft from alpine lakes and streams. Leave No Trace.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Bury waste 6-8 inches deep 200 feet from alpine lakes. Pack out toilet paper.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and down wood locally.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires permitted in cleared stone rings. Extinguish cold.
campfire_rules.seasonal_fire_bans: Subject to USFS dry summer fire bans.

access_and_road_conditions.road_type: Gravel mountain road (Hells Backbone Road / FS 154)
access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Graded gravel road with steep climbs and mountain pullouts.
access_and_road_conditions.vehicle_recommendation: CUV, SUV, or standard FWD car driven carefully in dry weather.

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2 bars 4G LTE on high 9,000-ft rim pullouts
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate - high subalpine plateau and aspen forest

seasonal_weather_effects.summer: Crisp 9,000-ft subalpine summer (70-76°F) escaping red rock desert heat below.
seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Spectacular golden aspen leaf display across Boulder Mountain in late September.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Closed to vehicle traffic due to deep snowpack.

dangers_and_hazards: High Altitude Weather Shifts & Freezing Night Temps
Narrow Mountain Road Drop-offs (Hells Backbone Bridge)
human_demographics_and_culture: High Southern Utah subalpine plateau, Boulder homesteading, and Capitol Reef conservation culture.

spiritual_and_folklore_data.nature_spirits_and_mythological_lore: Paiute traditions honor high Boulder Mountain ('The Mountain of Many Waters') as a sacred realm of clear alpine lakes and aspen groves.
spiritual_and_folklore_data.energetic_and_spiritual_features: 9,000-foot subalpine plateau overlooking 100 miles of red rock canyonlands generates an enchanting, majestic atmosphere.

nearby_hiking_trails.trail_name: Hells Backbone & Boulder Top Alpine Lake Trail
nearby_hiking_trails.features: 9,000-ft summit vistas over Capitol Reef, alpine trout lakes, golden aspen groves

public_reviews_summary: Cool 70-degree summer weather, breathtaking views over Southern Utah canyonlands, pristine trout lakes.
other_data: Carry warm clothing even in mid-summer as night temperatures drop near 40°F.
